verdict.rationale: Crawl4AI's own docs cover each part of the story: it returns clean Markdown directly from `crawler.arun()` or `crwl -o markdown`, and Fit Markdown and BM25 filtering strip noise from messy HTML. It renders JS-driven pages by executing scripts, waiting for dynamic content and simulating scrolling, and handles blocking with undetected browsers, proxies and automatic retry with fallback fetch. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration that the output is consistently clean and that anti-bot bypass works in practice (community evidence is only general praise, and one commenter notes bot mitigation still needs production attention).

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can get clean LLM-ready text directly instead of dealing with blocking, rendering, and messy HTML myself

citations.quote: Generate Clean Markdown: Perfect for RAG pipelines or direct ingestion into LLMs.
Fit Markdown: Heuristic-based filtering to remove noise and irrelevant parts for AI-friendly processing.
Dynamic Crawling: Execute JS and wait for async or sync for dynamic content extraction.
Undetected Browser Support: Bypass sophisticated bot detection systems
Automatic retry with proxy chain and fallback fetch function
